mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate, thereby increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 255.0 (a 12-month annualized inflation rate exceeding 5.0%) signals persistent inflation that triggers central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.0, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) and strong housing starts (HOUST > 1200.0) indicates robust consumer demand and confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through increased corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both UNRATE < 3.5% and HOUST > 1200.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 3.0% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 days as higher discount rates reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 3.0% and rising for 3 months, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by a high PAYEMS (above 149,000 thousand persons), consistently supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring a specific trigger condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 149,000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO reading below 105.0 (indicating a contraction in industrial production) signals weakening economic activity that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 105.0, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) and high labor force participation (PAYEMS > 149,000) indicates a tight labor market that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through elevated consumer spending and corporate hiring.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 149000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (INDPRO falling below 105.0 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.0 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.
